label: Core Concepts
desc: 15 interview questions covering Fundamentals, Star Schema, Fact Tables, Keys and more.

subs.label: Fundamentals
subs.desc: Data modeling in analytics is the process of structuring data so it can be queried reliably and efficiently for business questions.

subs.label: Star Schema
subs.desc: What is the difference between fact and dimension tables? What is a star schema and what are its benefits?

subs.label: Fact Tables
subs.desc: What are the main types of fact tables? What is a factless fact table?

subs.label: Keys
subs.desc: What is a surrogate key and when should you use it?

subs.label: Dimensions
subs.desc: Degenerate dimensions are identifiers stored directly in the fact table without a separate dimension table, such as order_id or invoice_number.

subs.label: SCD
subs.desc: SCD describes how you handle changes in dimension attributes over time (for example, a user changing address).

subs.label: Data Quality
subs.desc: How do you prevent double counting in analytical models? How do you validate a data model after changes?

subs.label: Data Vault
subs.desc: Data Vault is a modeling methodology designed for auditability, scalability, and flexibility when integrating many source systems, especially where schemas and sources change often.

label: NoSQL & Modern Analytics-Engineering Modeling
desc: 8 interview questions covering NoSQL, Analytics Engineering.

subs.label: NoSQL
subs.desc: Relational modeling starts from the data's structure and normalizes to avoid redundancy; NoSQL modeling starts from your application's access patterns and denormalizes deliberately so the most common queries need no joins.

subs.label: Analytics Engineering
subs.desc: What are dbt's staging, intermediate, and marts layers, and why keep them separate? What is the medallion architecture (bronze/silver/gold), and how does it relate to data modeling?

label: Advanced Dimension Patterns
desc: 6 interview questions covering Dimensions, Hierarchies, SCD.

subs.label: Dimensions
subs.desc: A role-playing dimension is a single physical dimension table used multiple times in the same fact table through different foreign keys and views, representing different roles it plays.

subs.label: Hierarchies
subs.desc: A ragged hierarchy is one where branches have different depths — an org chart where some employees report directly to the CEO and others sit five levels down.

subs.label: SCD
subs.desc: SCD Type 4 splits a dimension into a current-values table and a separate history table, rather than keeping both current and historical rows in one table with effective dates like Type 2.

label: Schema Evolution, Contracts & Relationships
desc: 7 interview questions covering Schema Evolution, Relationships, Fact Tables.

subs.label: Schema Evolution
subs.desc: Schema evolution is how a table's structure changes over time — new columns, renamed fields, changed types.

subs.label: Relationships
subs.desc: Cardinality describes how many instances of one entity relate to instances of another — one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many.

subs.label: Fact Tables
subs.desc: What questions should you ask before modeling a new fact table for a new business domain?
